description:
FOUND s501b (Opus, 2026-10-01) by the CPAN board run on Math-BigInt-2.005003 (the #2083 acceptance leg).  PRE-EXISTING in the sense that the code path is old, but NEWLY REACHABLE: on main a0899ba6 every Math::BigRat program died in the #2083 binding-stack recursion (UNIVERSAL::isa delegating to Math::BigFloat's isa override), so this answer was never seen; s501b's #2083 fix turns that crash into this SILENT WRONG answer.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s501b/p/rat3.pl in the s501b worktree; perl 5.40.3 vs PCL at s501b):
    use Math::BigRat;
    for my $s ("3", "49/4", "1/3", "0.5", "-7/2") { my $x = Math::BigRat->new($s); print "$s -> $x\n" }
    my $q = Math::BigRat->new(Math::BigInt->new(49), Math::BigInt->new(4)); print "obj -> $q\n";
  perl: 3 -> 3 / 49/4 -> 49/4 / 1/3 -> 1/3 / 0.5 -> 1/2 / -7/2 -> -7/2 / obj -> 49/4
  PCL : 3 -> 3 / 49/4 -> 1    / 1/3 -> 1   / 0.5 -> 1/2 / -7/2 -> -1   / obj -> 49/4
So only the "N/D" STRING spelling is wrong; the result looks like a truth value (1 / -1 = sign), i.e. something in BigRat::new's string branch (the `m|^\s*([+-]?[^/]+)\s*/\s*(.+?)\s*$|` split, or the `_trim`/`from_*` helpers) returns a boolean where perl returns the captured parts.  Cheap discriminating measurement (not taken): instrument a copy of Math/BigRat.pm's new() (the #2080 method) printing the two captures and the objects built from them.

IMPACT on the board (scratch/s501b/board-tree.log): bigratup.t floor/ceil/bsqrt rows, big_ap.t #3-#5/#15 ('inf'), bitwise-mbr.t (2601 not-ok) are the visible consequences -- these rows were all unreached (0 rows) on the base.

  and the two-object form -> 49/4.  (The first PCL run compiled Math::BigRat cold: 106 s.)

=== s543p (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-27, CODE 0ab08642) === Rosetta census (#2104): 0195-Check-Machin-like-formulas holds this cause.
NEUTRAL REPRODUCER (run on the tree):
    use Math::BigRat;
    my $a = Math::BigRat->new('1/2');
    my $b = Math::BigRat->new('1/3');
    print $a + $b, "\n";                                  # perl 5/6     PCL 2
    my $c = Math::BigRat->new(Math::BigInt->new(1), Math::BigInt->new(3));
    print $c + $c, "\n";                                  # perl 2/3     PCL 2/3   (the two-object form is right)
The program builds every fraction from an "N/D" string, so every rational is 1; with the strings replaced by the two-object form its first output line becomes identical and the rest differ by #5465 (an overloaded `/` handler run in list context: bdiv returns quotient and remainder).  frequency stays ordinary; the name is the evidence.

The reproducer is the one in the block above.

=== DONE (s543t) === (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28; cl/, WIP 5047d2af + be391add; generation v2-16600)
THE MEASUREMENT (taken first): Math::BigRat::new's string branch splits "N/D" with a two-group match, then calls Math::BigFloat->new($1, ...) and Math::BigFloat->new($2, ...); BigFloat::new runs matches of its OWN, and PCL's match state was one global, so the caller's $2 was the callee's.  REDUCED, nothing about rationals (scratch/s543t/p/m4-cap.pl): `sub inner { my $x = shift; $x =~ /^(\d+)$/ or return "no"; "in:$1" } if ("49/4" =~ m|^(\S+)/(\S+)$|) { inner($1); inner($2) }` -- perl in:49 in:4, PCL in:49 no.  = #932's SUB half (perl saves PL_curpm per sub).
FIX at the runtime's sub frame (rule 9a: nothing named BigRat): p-sub-frame wraps every sub body in %p-match-scope -- a lazy snapshot at the frame's first successful match (%p-match-record, the one writer), restored at the normal exit after the return value is copied (`return $1` is the callee's); details in #932's s543t note and docs/ir-spec.md "Match variables".
